The pursuit stretched across 17.9 miles, with speeds reaching between 100 and 120 miles per hour,
nearly striking two civilian vehicles and causing significant damage to four deputy patrol squads
as officers desperately tried to bring the vehicle to a stop. During the chase, the vehicle also sped
across an active airport runway at speeds exceeding 60 to 90 miles per hour, before tearing
through an agricultural field, causing more than $300 worth of damage to a farmer's property.
One deputy also suffered a wrist injury during the pursuit, though he was later medically cleared.
Ultimately, Chas Young was charged with felony, first degree recklessly endangering safety,
times four, vehicle fleeing, eluding an officer, possession of a firearm by convicted
felon, false imprisonment, possession of narcotic death, second offense, misdemeanor,
possession of controlled substance, resisting obstructing an officer, and criminal damage to property
times six. Almost all the charges are repeat offenses, and his cash bond was set at $200,000.
Eventually, he was found guilty due to a no-contest plea of all recklessly endangering safety counts,
possession of a firearm, fleeing eluding, possession of narcotic butt, resisting, possession of
controlled substance, and all criminal damage counts. Ultimately, he was sentenced to 12 years in the
Wisconsin State Prison, followed by 11 years of extended supervision.
As for the passenger, Alonzo, he was charged with felony, vehicle fleeing, eluding an officer,
party to a crime, possession of a firearm by convicted felon, possession of marijuana, possession of narcotic
tracts, battery threat to an officer, and he was subsequently released on a $10,000 cash bond.
Lastly, regarding the female passenger, there is no indication that her charges were ever officially filed,
suggesting the district attorney likely chose not to pursue them.
